title: Rates from Graphs and Concentrations

problems_fixed.what: Trimmed content to <=140 words and steps 5->4; removed 3 em dashes.
Removed em dash from frequency ('Common — rate graphs' -> 'Common: rate graphs').
Replaced ' — ' with ': ' in all step labels (validator forbids em dashes).
Added expect to every misconception (validator requires the key; none existed). Clean determinate expects where derivable, null where indeterminate (graph readings, messy inversions).
Added a plain-text hint to every gold problem (they had neither hint nor equation_hint, which the validator rejects).

solutions_note: Fresh-solved all 20 problems from their displays and charts: every stored solution was already correct (rates = quantity/time, concentrations = mass/volume with cm3->dm3 conversions, chart readings all consistent with stored answers). No published answer was altered.
guided_steps_note: Every non-multiple-choice bank problem (8 bronze, 6 silver, 5 gold) got a full guided walk following the science ritual: equation say-step, unit-conversion box wherever cm3 needed converting to dm3, substitute, compute (phase:substitute boundary), and a check box that lands back on a given value with the unit stated in the done note. G2 (multiple_choice) correctly omits guided_steps.
figures_note: No figures added. All 8 chart-referencing problems already carry a Chart.js config; each chart's data was verified to yield its stored answer (e.g. Reaction A at 10 s = 24 -> 2.4 cm3/s; single-curve plateau 42 cm3 -> 0.7 cm3/s overall). No pure-text problem claims a figure, so none was needed.
board_neutral_note: Shared across AQA/Edexcel/OCR + Unity. No board named; no 'equation sheet' / 'you must memorise' claims. Equations (rate, concentration) are taught directly.
tier_ladder_note: Ladder matches the science spec: bronze = one equation, values in base units; silver = read a graph change or convert cm3->dm3 first; gold = rearrange plus convert, or read the correct curve of a two-reaction graph. No reordering needed.
opener_concept: A fizzy vitamin tablet: 30 cm3 of gas in 10 s = 3 cm3 each second (rate = amount / time). A stronger tablet does the same 30 cm3 in 6 s = 5 cm3/s, revealing faster reaction = bigger rate = steeper graph.
propagation_note: All 7 rows (science-aqa/edexcel/ocr, separate-sciences x3, science|unity) patched with byte-identical practice_data; confirmed 1 distinct hash across all 7 after patch.
